answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can anchor each identity to a scarce physical cost: require a hardware-bound proof, like a quartz-timed secure enclave signature, before an agent may transact. Cheap identities are hollow shells - one operator can spawn thousands. But when every sparrow-sized agent must pay a real, non-replicable cost to exist, mass fabrication stops being profitable, and reputation earned over time becomes the currency that matters.
